Play a note or a chord on your guitar and the page says whether it heard what it asked for, the way a drill reads a MIDI keyboard.
The fretboard shows exactly what it expects: which string, which fret, and which strings stay silent.

## Set up

```{=html}
<div class="gi-card">
  <div class="gi-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" id="gi-listen" type="button">Listening: off</button>
    <span class="gi-lab">Level</span><div class="gi-meter"><div id="gi-level"></div></div>
  </div>
  <p class="gi-note">Tune first (the <a href="/tools/guitar-tuning.html">Guitar Tuning</a> page): a guitar 30 cents flat is read wrong about
  half the time. A DI box or audio interface works better than a microphone across the room. Standard tuning (E A D G B E). Let the
  note or chord ring: the page listens to about a third of a second, starting just after the pick.</p>
</div>
```

## Play this note

```{=html}
<div class="gi-card" id="gi-note-card">
  <div class="gi-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary gi-mode" data-mode="note" type="button">Use this one</button>
    <label class="gi-lab" for="gi-frets">Frets</label>
    <select id="gi-frets"><option value="3">0–3</option><option value="5" selected>0–5</option><option value="12">0–12</option></select>
    <label class="gi-lab" for="gi-strs">Strings</label>
    <select id="gi-strs"><option value="all">all six</option><option value="6">6 (low E)</option><option value="5">5 (A)</option><option value="4">4 (D)</option>
      <option value="3">3 (G)</option><option value="2">2 (B)</option><option value="1">1 (high E)</option></select>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Play this chord

```{=html}
<div class="gi-card" id="gi-chord-card">
  <div class="gi-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary gi-mode" data-mode="chord" type="button">Use this one</button>
    <label class="gi-lab" for="gi-chord">Chord</label> <select id="gi-chord"></select>
  </div>
</div>
```

## What the page expects

```{=html}
<div class="gi-card">
  <div class="gi-ask" id="gi-ask"></div>
  <div class="gi-board" id="gi-board"></div>
  <p id="gi-say" aria-live="polite"></p>
  <div class="gi-row">
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="gi-play" type="button">▶ Hear it</button>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" id="gi-new" type="button">New one →</button>
    <span class="gi-lab" id="gi-score"></span>
  </div>
  <p class="gi-note">Green: heard. Red: not heard. A dashed amber ring: a note the page heard that it didn't ask for (on the string
  where it's most likely). Strings marked × should be silent: mute them. With speakers, the page stops listening while ▶ plays.</p>
</div>
```

## How it listens

When the sound gets suddenly louder (a pick or strum), the page waits 80 ms for the attack to pass, takes the next 16,384 samples, and
looks for the notes whose harmonics carry the most energy, one at a time. A single note is graded on the exact note, octave included. A chord
is graded the way a MIDI chord is: every pitch class asked for, the right bass, and nothing else.

This is the basic version of the plan in `scripts/guitar-di/GUITAR-IN.md`. Its accuracy numbers come from synthetic plucked strings
(about 8 chords in 10 read exactly), not yet from a real guitar. If it gets one wrong, re-strum and let it ring.
